On persvati (certify-20261007T223016Z-2919327, 4 jobs, load 7.5) owner-host took 22.6 s with 18,129 prover steps: its time there is include and load, not proof, so the hbox figure needs its event split first (proof_cost.py on the gate manifest: slowest events). Two questions: (1) owner-host: which events or includes take the 130-500 s on hbox. The hazard-rule class (p-rule-class, train 14) already took fn-owner-log-reopen's guard from 43.7 s to 0.02 s, so measure at a post-train-14 sha. (2) image-world: must it recertify whenever any book in its closure changes, or can a gate check it against the world it includes (an include-only umbrella whose certificate is the conjunction of its includes')? tools/gate_walls.py (lane n-gate-time) keeps these as a standing row.
notes: P 2026-10-07 23:55, event split of converge-3's gate manifest (hbox .../native-c3-0b4d3b183/tree/build/acl2/certify-20261007T215044Z-2988778, load ~8): host/owner-host elapsed 129.97 s = ACL2 certify-book 81.17 s, of which INCLUDE-BOOK 79.22 s over ~400 includes (largest 3.0 s, catalog-may-seal), DEFUN 0.40 s, DEFTHM 0.05 s, prover steps 18,129; the other ~49 s is outside ACL2's event time (process start, certificate write, compile). books/image-world elapsed 164.20 s = certify-book 159.33 s, INCLUDE-BOOK 159.08 s (largest 2.17 s, ../host/owner-host; ~0.4 s per include), 0 steps. All fasls loaded (0 'Unable to load compiled file'). So neither is proof time: both are the time to load their include closure, and image-world's certificate certifies nothing but that the closure composes. Candidate moves: (a) image-world: a gate checks composition with the closure's installed certificates (certs.py install-umbrellas already composes the set) instead of certifying it, and it is certified once per convergence; (b) owner-host: its closure (~400 books) is the bar; the cuts are fewer includes (owner-host includes what the host calls; tools/host_check.py --books names the book per call) or a smaller certified world for host files.
